sentences.text: The name Rhoetosaurus means "Rhoetus lizard" and refers to a titan from Greek mythology.
This animal is estimated to have reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of 9 tonnes.
Heber Longman discovered the first fossils of Rhoetosaurus in 1924 at Durham Downs near Roma in Queensland.
The specific name brownei honors Arthur Browne, the station manager who provided the initial fossil fragments to Longman.
By 2012, the known fossil material included 40 vertebrae, parts of the pelvis, and much of the right hind limb.
To date, the tail tip, forelimbs, and skull of Rhoetosaurus have not been found.
Researchers suggest Rhoetosaurus might have had a clubbed tail due to its supposed relationship with Shunosaurus.
Longman initially classified Rhoetosaurus as a cetiosaurid based on advice from Friedrich von Huene due to its primitive nature.
A 2012 study placed Rhoetosaurus as a basal sauropod outside Eusauropoda, though its exact position remains debated, but confirmed it was not a Neosauropod.
Rhoetosaurus lived approximately 162 to 155 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
